references.text: Isaiah prophesies that even the captives of the mighty shall be taken from him, and that the Lord himself will fight against those who fight against his people – a direct parallel to the stronger one who overcomes the strong and takes his spoil.

Isaiah describes the Lord's suffering servant who will share the spoil with the strong, because he gave his life – a messianic prophecy about Christ as the stronger one who overcomes the strong and distributes the plunder.
Matthew's parallel passage where Jesus speaks of binding the strong man in order to plunder his house – the same parable about Jesus' power over Satan.

Mark's parallel passage where Jesus says that no one can enter a strong man's house and carry off his belongings unless he first binds the strong man – the same teaching about Jesus' victory over Satan.

Paul writes that Christ disarmed the rulers and authorities and made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them – this is the fulfillment of the stronger one taking the full armor of the strong and distributing the spoil.
John writes that the Son of God was revealed to destroy the works of the devil – this connects to the stronger one who overcomes the strong and takes from him all he relied on.
John assures believers that the one who is in them is greater than the one who is in the world – a confirmation that Christ is the stronger one who has overcome Satan.
Paul uses the image of God's full armor (panoplia), the same word as in Luke 11:22 regarding the strong man's armor – believers put on God's armor after Christ has taken the evil one's armor.
